title: the seeded line (the fibonacci line for pi, e, and the golden seed — in the bandgen way)

lesson.statement: my seeded line, for a seed c, stands at seed one and c under the sum rule: every later term is the sum of the two before it, and every term reads as the sum line's term at the n-minus-one index plus c times the sum line's term at the n index — my line's own skeleton, the consecutive pair, carries the seed's hat; the seed-one line is the sum line shifted by one and the seed-two line shifted by two, no other seed standing on my line a shift; and each term's own cassini, the product of the surrounding terms minus the square of the middle, is (minus one) to the n times (c squared minus c minus one), at the line end eighty-four

the golden seed stands off the line between the one and the two, named by the equation x squared equals x plus one, never by a digit; the line for the golden seed is the golden seed to the n power — the term at the n-plus-p index is the term at the n index times the golden seed to the p power, that multiplier never one, so the line advances without collapse and without return; its integer shadow runs on the skeleton, the term at the n index reading as the sum line's n-minus-one term plus the golden seed times its n term; and its cassini is silent, the weight c squared minus c minus one exactly zero exactly at the golden equation, at the line end eighty-four

theorems.statement: the seeded line of my store is filed of record: the sequence for a seed c stands at seed one and c under the sum rule, every later term the sum of the two before it, reading on the sum line's own skeleton as the n-minus-one term plus c times the n term, the seed-one and seed-two lines the sum line itself shifted and no other seed a shift; the cassini weight is (minus one) to the n times (c squared minus c minus one), silent exactly at the golden equation; the line for the golden seed is the power of the golden seed, advancing without collapse and without return, its shadow on the skeleton; every constant stands off the floor, named by position and by the equation, never by a digit; filed on the line, at the line end eighty-four
